title: Morning Edition
dek: Air-traffic infrastructure under scrutiny; Atlantic migration; autonomous-weapons rules; and the meaning of wonder.

lead_story.headline: FAA outage renews fight over air-traffic modernization
lead_story.summary: After a nationwide flight grounding linked by officials to overloaded communications equipment, the administration is asking Congress for $50 billion to overhaul air traffic control. Lawmakers are questioning how earlier modernization funding was used; the precise failure sequence remains under investigation.
lead_story.why_it_matters: A single communications failure disrupted travel nationwide and exposed the difficulty of modernizing safety-critical infrastructure while it stays operational.

items.headline: Nearly 2,200 migrants arrive in Spain's Canary Islands over two days
items.summary: Spanish rescue services reported a sharp surge in Atlantic crossings, with 1,324 people assisted from 14 dinghies and most arriving at El Hierro. The dangerous route has been under increasing pressure.
items.why_it_matters: The crossings expose the gap between border policy, rescue capacity and conditions that drive migration across one of the world's deadliest sea routes.

items.headline: Governments debate binding rules for autonomous weapons
items.summary: Diplomats meeting in Geneva are considering whether to launch negotiations on weapons capable of selecting and attacking targets without human direction. Several countries support talks, but consensus rules allow opponents to block progress.
items.why_it_matters: The central question is whether meaningful human control and accountability can be made enforceable before autonomous targeting becomes routine.

items.headline: Starship returns from orbit to launch site in reuse milestone
items.summary: SpaceX recovered the Starship upper stage at its launch pad following an orbital flight, a step toward making both rocket stages reusable. The booster was not recovered in the same test.
items.why_it_matters: The achievement reduces one major engineering uncertainty, but reliable repeat flights and orbital refueling remain separate challenges.

items.headline: New AI traffic-management tool faces scrutiny after unrelated FAA outage
items.summary: The FAA and its contractor say the SMART advisory system was not involved in the communications failure. Congressional critics nevertheless want an audit of its reliability, training and oversight.
items.why_it_matters: Safety-critical AI needs independently testable boundaries even when a specific incident has a different cause.

items.headline: Older catch-up: ancient Assyrian letters read without opening clay envelopes
items.summary: A scanning technique has allowed researchers to decipher correspondence sealed inside 3,800-year-old clay envelopes from Kanesh, preserving the artifacts intact.
items.why_it_matters: Non-destructive imaging can reveal ordinary ancient lives without sacrificing the objects that carry their words.

items.headline: A Fairfax school marketplace brings together neighborhood makers
items.summary: Robinson Secondary School hosted a November 15 marketplace for local craft vendors and small businesses, including pottery and handmade goods. The event was advertised as a community shopping gathering; attendance has not been independently confirmed.
items.why_it_matters: A small seasonal example of a school serving as a place for neighbors to meet and share handmade work.

items.headline: Why history and philosophy need room for wonder
items.summary: Historian Marnie Hughes-Warrington argues that professional history loses something essential when it treats surprise, uncertainty and the strangeness of the past as embarrassments to be explained away.
items.why_it_matters: Wonder can be an intellectual discipline: it reveals assumptions hidden by tidy accounts of the past.

worth_your_time.headline: What Gödel's incompleteness changed about the limits of knowledge
worth_your_time.summary: An Aeon essay traces the ambition of David Hilbert's mathematical program and the disruption caused by Kurt Gödel's incompleteness results, then asks what those limits do and do not imply about knowledge.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: The history is a caution against overextending a formal mathematical result into claims about every human question.
